lens: Clinical gait / brain-body science, via interpretability of biosignal (pose) representations: which clinically meaningful gait scalars a self-supervised skeleton world model retains versus discards, and what that says about using SSL body-models for clinical gait analysis. Framed strictly as a measurement-and-representation study, not a diagnostic-performance study.
title: The Representation Forgets the Side: What a Self-Supervised Skeleton JEPA Keeps and Discards for Clinical Gait Scalars
one_sentence_question: When a self-supervised skeleton JEPA learns gait, does it retain the clinically meaningful gait scalars (cadence, stride time, double-support fraction, swing/stance asymmetry, step-length symmetry) that markerless pose encodes essentially for free, or does its left-right-symmetric prediction objective systematically discard the signed asymmetry that the most clinically discriminative gait biomarkers live on?
why_novel: This is not another 'SSL beats baselines on gait classification' paper, which is indefensible here (1-2 source videos per clinical class, single dataset, all current results transductive). The novel move is to reframe an already-verified negative result as positive evidence about the inductive bias of JEPA-style latent prediction on a bilaterally symmetric body model. Concretely: the signed-laterality probe shows the trained encoder exposes LESS signed left-minus-right asymmetry (R2 = -0.187) than an untrained random-init encoder (R2 = +0.147), while raw coordinates solve the same probe trivially (R2 ≈ 1.0), sign-consistency is at chance (0.5), and an anatomical mirror does not flip the axis (mirror slope -0.343). That is, training actively removed laterality rather than merely failing to learn it. The mechanistic chain is identifiable in the design itself: a bilaterally symmetric masking whitelist (both shoulders/hips/knees/ankles/heels/foot-indexes), VICReg covariance decorrelation, and a sign-free mean/std pooled readout that discards temporal order by construction. The clinical significance is that swing/stance asymmetry and step-length symmetry are canonical, literature-validated biomarkers for post-stroke and Parkinsonian gait, so the representation forgets exactly the axis clinicians measure. The paper contributes (1) a principled axis-by-axis decomposition of representation content into laterality-free temporal scalars (cadence, stride time, double-support) versus laterality-dependent scalars (swing/stance asymmetry, step-length symmetry), (2) a pre-registered informative-null protocol that converts a small transductive dataset into a crisp statement about what the objective chooses to encode, and (3) a prescriptive conclusion: representation objectives must be matched to the clinical axis of interest, and symmetric-prediction world models will not, by default, preserve directional asymmetry.
workshop_fit: Directly targets two named workshop bullets: 'interpretability of biosignal representations' (the informative null is a precise, falsifiable statement about what the representation forgot, not a post-hoc saliency story) and 'applications to health and clinical diagnosis' (the five scalars are the actual clinical constructs, and the finding warns which biomarkers an SSL body-model will or will not retain). It also hits 'measuring whether pretraining helps: probing and downstream evaluation' and 'self-supervised learning for biosignals'. It fits the 2026 edition's motor-side emphasis: gait is the movement loop, and signed laterality/swing-stance asymmetry is a motor-control-relevant axis. Pose extracted from video is explicitly included as a biosignal, and the GAVD dataset plus markerless-pose measurement validity (Hii et al. 2023, MediaPipe-vs-Vicon ICC > 0.75) grounds the measurement layer.

decisive_experiments.question: Can the five clinical scalars be computed reliably from the raw markerless pose caches, with real time units?
decisive_experiments.method: Use the raw pose npz caches (sequence shape (frames,33,4), frame_numbers, and per-video fps present in the extraction report, e.g. 23.976/29.97/30.0), not the 64-frame model input. Implement a deterministic, pre-registered gait-event detector (heel strike = local minima of forward ankle/heel progression; toe-off = swing initiation) to yield cadence (steps/min), stride time (s), double-support fraction, swing/stance asymmetry index, and step-length symmetry (left/right ratio, not absolute meters). Report per-scalar reliability: inter-stride agreement within a clip, sensitivity to landmark noise, and a cross-check of stride time against the autocorrelation period of ankle separation.
decisive_experiments.expected_outcome: Cadence and stride time are reliable (temporal, robust to 2D depth error); step-length symmetry and swing/stance asymmetry are reliable on side-view sequences only (left/right is well-defined there); double-support fraction is the noisiest (requires precise toe-off in 2D) and is reported as a secondary target with a stated reliability floor.
decisive_experiments.falsifies: If even cadence/stride time are unreliable, the clinical-scalar premise fails and the paper must fall back to normalized-time representation diagnostics only.

decisive_experiments.question: Under source-video grouping, how well do raw kinematic features versus frozen S-JEPA features decode each scalar, and does the S-JEPA advantage/disadvantage depend on whether the scalar is laterality-free or laterality-dependent?
decisive_experiments.method: Reuse source_disjoint_probe (GroupKFold on video_id, ridge with inner alpha selection inside training sources only). Decode each of the five scalars from (a) hand-crafted raw kinematic features and (b) the frozen 384-d pooled S-JEPA embedding, plus (c) an untrained-encoder floor. Report per-source R2 and per-source dots, never only a pooled number. Label the frozen-encoder lane as transductive (encoder saw every row).
decisive_experiments.expected_outcome: Laterality-free temporal scalars (cadence, stride time) decode comparably from raw and S-JEPA (global rhythm survives in joint statistics); laterality-dependent scalars (swing/stance asymmetry, step-length symmetry) decode strongly from raw pose but collapse to near-chance/negative R2 from S-JEPA features. This is the headline divergence and mirrors the laterality probe.
decisive_experiments.falsifies: If S-JEPA also decodes the laterality-dependent scalars, the informative null does not generalize beyond the specific probe construction and the story narrows substantially.

decisive_experiments.question: Is the signed-laterality failure a property of the training objective rather than an artifact of one run, one probe, or the pooled readout?
decisive_experiments.method: Formalize the already-verified nb_05a result as the mechanistic anchor: learned lane A R2 = -0.187, raw-null lane B R2 ≈ 1.0, untrained-encoder floor lane C R2 = +0.147 (floor beats trained), side-agnostic control lane D R2 = -0.014 (sign-specific, control passes), sign consistency 0.5, mirror slope -0.343 with no sign flip. Connect each number to a named design choice: symmetric masking whitelist, VICReg covariance decorrelation, sign-free mean/std pooling, and the label-aware group loss compressing condition-level variation.
decisive_experiments.expected_outcome: The four-lane structure proves the loss is specific to SIGN, not to per-side magnitude (D passes), and that training reduced laterality below the random-init floor (C > A), which is the strongest possible statement that the objective actively discarded it rather than failing to learn it.
decisive_experiments.falsifies: If side-agnostic lane D also failed, the claim would reduce to 'pooling is sign-blind', a far weaker (pooling-only) story; D passing is what pins the effect on the learned representation.

decisive_experiments.question: Does the asymmetry-null persist when the encoder is retrained with held-out source videos excluded, or is it an artifact of the single transductive checkpoint?
decisive_experiments.method: Retrain the encoder inside source-video-disjoint outer folds (full curriculum ~20 min, a single stage a few minutes, per the audit's measured retraining cost), excluding held-out source videos before any fitting, then re-run E1/E2 on held-out sources. With only 1 canonical normal video this is feasible because the 17 added-normal videos supply normal-side sources; report every fold separately and label any remaining frozen-checkpoint result transductive.
decisive_experiments.expected_outcome: Cadence/stride-time decoding survives fold-local retraining (cheap, global temporal regularity); signed-asymmetry decoding stays at/above the untrained floor, confirming the null is a property of the objective, not the specific run.
decisive_experiments.falsifies: If the asymmetry-null disappears under fold-local retraining, the honest paper downgrades it to 'artifact of the current transductive checkpoint' and refocuses on the scalar-decoding gap.

decisive_experiments.question: Do the decoded scalars move in literature-predicted directions, and are any decoding results explained by nuisance channels rather than gait?
decisive_experiments.method: As a one-paragraph illustrative check (not a claim), compare per-condition decoded scalar distributions to published directions (PD: reduced stride, increased cadence/double-support; stroke/CP: increased asymmetry) with a leave-one-source-out sensitivity for the 2-video classes. In parallel, run nuisance controls: predict landmark coverage and extraction provenance from the same features, so a scalar 'win' that merely tracks coverage or the canonical-vs-added-normal path is exposed.
decisive_experiments.expected_outcome: A split, directionally-plausible result at best (step/rhythm scalars track literature; asymmetry scalars do not because the representation lacks them), reported with explicit small-n caveats; nuisance controls show raw-pose scalar decoding is gait-driven while any S-JEPA scalar decoding is not provenance-driven.
decisive_experiments.falsifies: A null here is acceptable and expected; it is explicitly not the paper's load-bearing claim.

effort_and_feasibility: Three days is feasible because the expensive parts already exist or are cheap. The pose caches preserve frame_numbers and per-video fps, so real-time scalars are computable without re-extraction; the gait-event detector is standard (heel-strike/toe-off from ankle/heel trajectories) and is a 0.5-1 day implementation plus a reliability audit. Scalar decoding reuses source_disjoint_probe (GroupKFold ridge with inner alpha selection) and the laterality feature builders already in the repo, so E1/E2 are a few hours of glue plus plotting once scalars exist. The informative null is already computed and saved (nb_05a + idea5_signed_laterality_result.json), so E2 is re-framing, not new compute. The only real compute is E3 fold-local retraining: ~20 min for a full 600-epoch curriculum and a few minutes per stage on this machine, so 2-3 source-disjoint folds fit in one day. The dominant cost is writing and figures for a 5-page paper. The main scope risk is that E3 (strict fold-local retrain) needs proposal 01's split harness, which is only partially built; the fallback that preserves honesty is to keep E1/E2 as clearly-labeled transductive descriptive probes and present E3 as a 2-fold confirmation.
main_risks: Claim ceiling: 1-2 source videos per clinical class, one dataset, single training seed, and transductive frozen checkpoints mean NO diagnostic, disease-detection, or patient-generalization claim is defensible; every probe must be labeled transductive unless fold-local retraining is completed, and folder labels must stay dataset annotations, not diagnoses.

Measurement risk: single-camera 2D pose cannot recover absolute step length in meters (z is rough relative depth), left/right can be ambiguous on non-side views, and double-support fraction needs precise toe-off that is noisy in 2D; mitigated by using symmetry/asymmetry as ratios, restricting laterality claims to side-view sequences, and reporting per-scalar reliability with a stated floor.

Readout confound: the 384-d pooled vector discards temporal order by construction, so a cadence/stride-time failure could be a pooling artifact rather than an encoder failure; mitigated by adding an untrained floor and, if time permits, a token-level/temporal readout so 'encoder forgot' versus 'pooling threw away' is separated.

Reviewer sees the null as 'obvious given symmetric masking + mean/std pooling' and undervalues it; mitigated because the floor-beats-trained result (untrained +0.147 > trained -0.187) and the passing side-agnostic control make it a non-trivial statement about training dynamics, not just pooling.

Provenance confound: the canonical normal path (1 video) and added-normal path (17 videos) differ in extraction/annotation; scalar decoding could leak coverage/quality rather than gait, so missingness and provenance controls are mandatory and any 'win' that tracks them is discarded.

Five-page pressure forces dropping either the fold-local retrain or the construct-validity check; the priority order is scalar decoding + informative null first, fold-local confirmation second, clinical direction check last and explicitly illustrative.
paper_outline_5p: Page 1 (Intro + claim): Pose as a biosignal; clinical gait biomarkers (cadence, stride time, double-support, swing/stance asymmetry, step-length symmetry) are what clinicians measure; self-supervised body-models are being pushed toward clinical use, but what do they actually retain? State the one-sentence question and the honest claim ceiling up front (no diagnosis, no generalization claim). Figure 1: the two-panel teaser - raw pose decodes signed asymmetry at R2 ~1.0, learned S-JEPA features at R2 -0.187 (below the untrained floor). Page 2 (Method): 1-2 lines on GAVD (96 canonical seq/18 videos + 63 added-normal/17 videos) and MediaPipe pose; the scalar definitions and deterministic event detector (real time units from frame_numbers/fps); the S-JEPA recap in one paragraph (latent CE, EMA target, VICReg, symmetric 12-landmark masking, label-aware group loss after Stage 0, 384-d mean/std pooling); the probe protocol (GroupKFold-by-video ridge with inner alpha selection, untrained-encoder floor, raw-kinematic baseline, side-agnostic control, missingness/provenance controls). Page 3 (Results 1-2): Table + per-source dot plots of scalar decodability, split into laterality-free (cadence, stride time: S-JEPA ~ raw) versus laterality-dependent (swing/stance asymmetry, step-length symmetry: raw strong, S-JEPA ~0); then the formalized informative null (four laterality lanes, mirror non-flip, floor-beats-trained). Page 4 (Results 3 + mechanism): fold-local source-disjoint retrain (or clearly-labeled transductive) showing the null persists; the mechanistic account tying the null to symmetric masking + covariance decorrelation + sign-free pooling + group loss; a brief illustrative construct-validity direction check with explicit caveats. Page 5 (Discussion): what this means for clinical biosignal SSL - representation objectives must be matched to the clinical axis of interest, and symmetric-prediction world models will not by default preserve directional asymmetry; a limitations table (single seed, tiny classes, transductive unless retrained, 2D depth limits, folder-labels-not-diagnoses); a prescriptive, reusable takeaway: always probe the signed-asymmetry axis when evaluating a body-model for clinical gait.
recommendation: Adopt this direction as the workshop paper. It is the only lens that converts the project's two strongest, already-verified assets (the signed-laterality INFORMATIVE NULL and the reusable source-grouped probing code) plus one cheap new asset (real-time clinical scalar extraction from the fps-bearing pose caches) into a defensible, novel, 3-day-feasible story. Execute in this order: (1) build and reliability-audit the five-scalar extractor; (2) run source-grouped raw-vs-S-JEPA scalar decoding and the untrained floor; (3) re-frame the laterality null as the mechanistic centerpiece with the floor-beats-trained and side-agnostic controls; (4) attempt 2-3 fold-local source-disjoint retrains for an honest generalization garnish, falling back to explicit transductive labeling if time runs out; (5) add missingness/provenance controls and a one-paragraph illustrative construct-validity check. Hold the claim line: no diagnostic or generalization claims, folder labels are annotations, and every number is reported per source with the transductive status stated. Do not attempt SOTA classification or a diagnostic framing - they are indefensible with this cohort and would sink an otherwise clean, insightful interpretability result.
